source.title: Training Object Detectors With Noisy Data

record.tranche_reason: Tests how label noise affects object detector performance using controlled label corruption, but does not measure training error or whether the detector fits random labels.
record.gate_note: The study reports AP under several label-noise conditions and compares co-teaching methods. These results bear on noisy-label test performance, but do not establish training-set fit, chance-level test error, or the claim’s other training behaviors.
record.test_reason: Section III uses V6's real-patterns-before-noise premise to justify co-teaching, citing Arpit et al. The study evaluates detector AP and mitigation performance, without measuring memorization or learning order. AP under partial label corruption does not establish V4's perfect training fit and degradation toward chance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: label noise affects CNN object detector performance, and modified per-object co-teaching mitigates its effects in the tested settings. Simultaneous training of two networks constrains model choice, and improvement requires hyperparameter tuning.
record.recipe_differences: Studies object detection under several forms of label noise and evaluates co-teaching; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and probability; co-teaching formulation; test set (automatic labels versus hand-labelled subset).

fits_no_version.finding: Table I reports detector AP under several corruption types. Whole-image pair noise lowers AP from 0.629 to 0.506 and 0.385 at probabilities 0.25 and 0.5; training-set fit is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial label corruption can reduce held-out object detection AP, with effects depending on corruption type and probability.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables II–III show per-object co-teaching improves AP over plain training in the reported comparisons and usually exceeds standard co-teaching.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selecting low-loss updates separately by object and loss component can improve object detection performance with noisy training labels.

record.problems: The study reports AP rather than training error or memorization; the KITTI table text is flattened, and results are limited to the reported detector, dataset splits, noise types, and probabilities.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted because reported outcomes concern AP under noisy labels or co-teaching comparisons, and do not measure any claim version's named behavior. Table I–III report the AP and Max F1 comparisons.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and steadily increasing test error toward chance. Reported AP at noise probabilities 0, 0.25, and 0.5 does not establish this behavior.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels; this is a premise of the method, without direct temporal measurements.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to uses_without_test/T4 and remove V4's tested_not_extracted designation. Empty rows are appropriate; the AP and mitigation results were explicitly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, with test error at chance and no training changes.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and how convergence changes with corrupted-label fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper measures test-set AP under label noise, but does not report training-set fit, perfect training accuracy, or whether test error rises toward chance while remaining signal is captured.
Whether regularization, dropout, augmentation, or their removal affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether true-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
